translation_en: Aishah said they used to salt sacrificial meat and bring it to the Prophet in Medina. He said, Do not eat it for more than three days. This was not a binding command; he wanted them to feed others from it, and Allah knows best. The report is from Ismail bin Abdullah, his brother, Sulayman, Yahya bin Said, Amrah bint Abd al-Rahman, and Aishah. Aishah said the instruction was not an irrevocable command.

Abu Ubaid said he attended the Eid of Sacrifice with Umar bin al-Khattab. Umar prayed before the sermon, then told the people the Messenger of Allah had forbidden fasting on the two Eids: one is the day you end your fast, and the other is the day you eat your sacrifices. Abu Ubaid attended the Eid prayer with Umar, who delivered this warning after praying and before giving the sermon.

Abu Ubaid said he later attended a Friday with Uthman bin Affan. It was a day when two festivals coincided. Uthman prayed before the sermon, then said people from the outskirts could stay for Friday prayer if they wished, or could leave if they wished.

Abu Ubaid said he later attended with Ali bin Abi Talib. Ali prayed before the sermon and told the people that the Messenger of Allah had forbidden eating sacrificial meat for more than three days. Maamar also reported this from al-Zuhri, from Abu Ubaid.

Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah said, Eat from the sacrificial animals for three days. When Abdullah left Mina, he would eat with oil because of the meat of the animals offered for pilgrimage. Abdullah followed this practice when leaving Mina because of the meat of the sacrificial animals.

Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah said, Whoever drinks wine in this world and does not repent of it will be deprived of it in the Hereafter. The report is narrated by Nafi from Abdullah bin Umar.

Abu Huraira reported that on the night the Prophet was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem, two cups, one of wine and one of milk, were brought to him. He looked at them and took the milk. Gabriel said, Praise belongs to Allah who guided you to the natural way; had you taken the wine, your community would have gone astray. Other transmitters also related this from al-Zuhri.

Anas said, I heard from the Messenger of Allah something that no one else will tell you. Among the signs of the Hour are widespread ignorance, little knowledge, widespread adultery, and drinking wine; men will become few and women numerous, until one man is responsible for fifty women.

Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said, An adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, and a person does not drink wine while drinking it as a believer. A thief does not steal while he is a believer. Abu Bakr used to add that a person does not seize valuable plunder while people look on, doing so as a believer. Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet said a person does not commit adultery, drink wine, or steal while doing so as a believer. Ibn Shihab said Abd al-Malik bin Abi Bakr related that Abu Bakr used to add: a person does not seize valuable public plunder while people look on, doing so as a believer.
Ibn Umar said wine was forbidden when there was none of it in Medina. The report was transmitted by al-Hasan bin Sabah, from Muhammad bin Sabiq, from Malik bin Mighwal, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar.

Anas said wine was forbidden when little grape wine could be found in Medina. Most of their wine was made from unripe and ripe dates. Anas said wine was forbidden while grape wine was scarce in Medina. Their usual drink was made from unripe and ripe dates.

Umar stood on the pulpit and said the prohibition of wine had been revealed. It is made from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley. Wine is whatever overwhelms the mind. Umar listed grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley as the five sources. He defined wine as whatever overcomes the mind.

Anas said he was serving Abu Ubaidah, Abu Talhah, and Ubayy bin Kaab a drink made from ripe and dried dates. Someone came and said wine had been forbidden. Abu Talhah told Anas to pour it away, and he did. Anas was pouring the drink when the news of prohibition came. Abu Talhah instructed him to pour it out, and Anas did so.

Anas said he was standing and serving his uncles, the youngest among them, with a drink made from dates. Someone announced that wine had been forbidden. They told him to overturn it, so he did. Asked what their drink had been, Anas said ripe and unripe dates. Abu Bakr bin Anas said it had been their wine, and Anas did not object. One of Anas's companions also heard him say it had been their wine at the time.

Bakar bin Abdullah reported from Anas that when wine was forbidden, the wine of that time was made from unripe and ripe dates. Anas reported that the wine at that time consisted of unripe and ripe dates.

Aishah was asked about bit, a drink made from honey. The Messenger of Allah said, Every intoxicating drink is unlawful. Aishah reported that the Prophet gave a general rule for every drink that intoxicates.

Aishah was asked about bit, the honey drink that people in Yemen used to drink. The Messenger of Allah said, Every intoxicating drink is unlawful. Bit was honey nabidh, a fermented honey drink consumed by people in Yemen. The Prophet gave the same rule: every intoxicating drink is forbidden.
The Prophet said, Do not prepare fermented drinks in gourds or pitch-coated vessels. Abu Huraira used to add the hantom and naqir vessels to this list.

Umar preached from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah and said wine had been forbidden. It is made from five things: grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and honey. Wine is whatever overwhelms the mind. Umar said there were three matters he wished the Messenger had clarified before leaving them: the inheritance of a grandfather, kalalah, and some forms of usury. He was asked about a drink made from rice in Sind. He said that drink had not existed in the time of the Prophet—or, he said, in Umar's time. Hajjaj reported from Hammad, from Abu Hayyan, that raisins were named in place of grapes.
Umar said wine is made from five things: raisins, dates, wheat, barley, and honey. Umar's list here gives raisins, dates, wheat, barley, and honey as the five things from which wine is made.

Hisham bin Ammar reported from Abu Amir—or Abu Malik—al-Ashari, who swore that he heard the Prophet say some people in his community would treat unlawful sexual relations, silk, wine, and musical instruments as lawful. Some people would settle beside a prominent hill with their livestock. A needy person would come asking them for something, and they would say, Come back tomorrow. Allah would cause the hill to collapse on them and transform others into apes and pigs until the Day of Resurrection.

Sahl said Abu Usayd al-Saidi invited the Messenger of Allah to his wedding. Abu Usayd's wife, who was the bride, served them. She said, Do you know what I gave the Messenger of Allah to drink? At night I soaked dates for him in a small vessel.

Jabir said the Messenger of Allah forbade certain containers. The Ansar said they needed them, and he said, Then do without them. Khalifah reported the same chain and wording, adding that the Prophet had forbidden vessels. Jabir said the Messenger prohibited the vessels, but the Ansar told him they had to use them. He replied, Then do without them. Khalifah also transmitted the report from Yahya bin Said, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Salim bin Abi al-Jad, from Jabir, and added that the Prophet had forbidden the containers.

Abdullah bin Amr said when the Prophet forbade certain water containers, people told him not everyone could find a waterskin. He allowed them to use unpitched earthen jars. Abdullah bin Amr reported that when the Prophet prohibited the water-skins, people said not everyone could find one. The Prophet then permitted unpitched jars.

Ali reported that the Prophet forbade making fermented drinks in gourds and pitch-coated vessels. Uthman also narrated this from Jarir, from al-Amash. Ali reported the prohibition of using gourds and pitch-coated containers for fermented drinks. Uthman also reported the wording from Jarir, from al-Amash.

Aishah said she told al-Aswad that the Prophet had forbidden her household to prepare fermented drinks in gourds and pitch-coated vessels. Al-Aswad asked whether she had also mentioned jars and hantom vessels. She replied that she was only telling him what she had heard; should she report what she had not heard?

Abdullah bin Abi Awfa reported that the Prophet forbade the green jar. He was asked whether they could drink from a white one, and he said no. The Prophet prohibited the green jar. Abdullah bin Abi Awfa was also asked whether people could use the white jar, and he said no.

Sahl bin Sad said Abu Usayd al-Saidi invited the Prophet to his wedding. The bride served them that day and said, Do you know what I soaked for the Messenger of Allah? At night I soaked dates for him in a small vessel. The bride prepared a date infusion overnight in a small vessel and served it to the Messenger of Allah at the wedding feast.

Ibn Abbas was asked about badhiq, a drink made from grape juice. He said Muhammad came before badhiq; whatever intoxicates is forbidden. Someone said, It is a lawful, wholesome drink. Ibn Abbas replied, Nothing lies beyond what is lawful and wholesome except what is unlawful and impure.

Aishah said the Prophet liked sweet foods and honey. Aishah reported this about the Prophet's favorite foods. The narration is transmitted by Abdullah bin Abi Shaybah, from Abu Usamah, from Hisham bin Urwah, from his father, from Aishah.
